Priya K.: Heads up 1 I'm planning a 10-week remote stint in Costa Rica starting 2024-08-01 (family coming). Im currently US-homebase. Questions: do I need to change homebase for 10 weeks? How will WFH stipend be handled if I'm remote 100% from CR for that period? Also, any customs/VAT on shipping company laptop + docking station? And health insurance while abroad for >30 days?

Nadia (People Ops): Thanks for flagging! Short: submit the Location Change form (link) and select "temporary remote abroad". For short stints we usually keep homebase the same unless payroll/legal flags nexus. Stipend: we pro-rate for temporary remote stints; payroll will confirm currency/payment.
https://redwoodintra/people-ops/location-change

Sam (Payroll): Tagging payroll: if homebase remains US, stipend stays USD and paid as usual but we record the CR days for tax nexus reporting. If homebase is switched to CR, stipend would convert to CRC and tax/withholding rules change. For 10 weeks typical approach: treat as transient remote; prorate by calendar days in pay period: stipend_payment = base_stipend * (remote_days / workdays_in_period). We'll run numbers after form.

Ivy (Benefits): Health: company medical plans have limited international coverage. >30 days may require a short-term international plan or evidence of coverage. Please DM benefits your travel dates & family composition. Also check dependents' visa/insurance requirements.

Marco (Legal): Quick legal note: Costa Rica can create employer reporting obligations if the employee performs work from within CR for a sustained period. 10 weeks is usually below thresholds that create local employer obligations, but we need exact dates and to confirm no contractual work for CR entities. We'll confirm after payroll review.

Priya K.: Shipping gear: laptop + docking station. Any customs/brokerage fees? I'm happy to pay if necessary but want to understand taxable benefit risk.

Customs Bot: Automated: Equipment shipments to CR often incur import duties and VAT (approx 13%) if not covered by temporary import rules. If device stays >6 months, it's more likely to be assessed. Coordinate with Ops for temporary carnet or ask IT for local pickup options.

Sam (Payroll): Also note: if company pays shipping or pays duties, that amount can be considered a taxable benefit in the US. We'll provide an estimate once you confirm shipping method. If you reimburse the company for duties, that avoids taxable benefit.

Nadia (People Ops): Action items: 1) Priya submit Location Change form today; 2) DM benefits (Ivy) passport + family DOBs; 3) DM payroll (Sam) preferred shipping option (company ship vs personal ship + expense). We'll queue a 20-min cross-functional check once form's in.

Priya K.: Thanks all 10 I'll submit form today and DM details. One more Q: does remote abroad time affect my WFH kit replacement eligibility (I have a pending monitor replacement)?

Ivy (Benefits): Equipment eligibility unchanged by location, but shipping constraints apply. If monitor needs replacement while abroad we may require local purchase + expense submission.

Marco (Legal): If anything changes on employment taxes or local registration, we'll notify you within 5 business days of case intake.

Customs Bot: Ticket created: CB-9122 (CR equipment shipping advisory). Expected ops follow-up 3 business days.

Priya K.: Appreciate it  Submitted the form and attached tentative dates. DMing passports and shipping preference now.
